newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bonds hit new record high.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bonds hit new record high.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended with yields at record lows on Wednesday, supported by a positive sentiment on other foreign markets and strong expectations of a rate cut at tomorrow's Bank of Spain repo auction.
"If the Bank of Spain does nothing, the market will think they don't approve of the 97 budget," a dealer at Fimat said.
Furthermore, a 25 bp cut would disappoint the market.
"In that case (of a 25 bp move) the market will go down, specially at the three-year part of the curve," another dealer said.
At close the benchmark 3-year bond was trading at 101.97, yielding 6.88 percent, versus 101.67 yesterday.
But if the BoS does reduce the repo rate 50 basis points or more the "the shorter end will gain most", he added.
The 10-year spread over German Bunds is back were it was at the end of last week when Aznar's government presented the budget, at 177 basis points.
"The general mood is still very positive," a dealer said.
"Even a bigger rate cut will be considered positive. Nobody could fear this is the last one of the cycle".
The central bank has cut its key money market rate five times this year, from 9.00 percent to 7.25 percent.
